capabilities.capability: Project-level .claude/settings.json hooks activate mid-session via a file watcher
capabilities.status: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED — documented behavior contradicts this environment's empirical behavior
capabilities.evidence: The same live doc fetch states: 'Direct edits to hooks in settings files are normally picked up automatically by the file watcher' — i.e. dynamic mid-session reload IS the documented default for the general Claude Code CLI product. Empirically, however, two separate tests in THIS session — immediately after writing .claude/settings.json, and again ~2 minutes and several tool calls later — both found the expected ledger directory was never created. Re-tested specifically because the new documentation contradicted the earlier empirical result, rather than accepting either claim alone.
capabilities.captureMechanism: live doc fetch + two independent empirical negative tests, deliberately spaced apart in time
limitations: The most likely explanation is that this session runs in a managed remote/CCR execution environment (stated explicitly in this session's own system context), which may not run the same file-watcher process the interactive CLI docs describe — not that hooks are unsupported generally.

Not confirmed which of several possibilities applies: no file watcher in this harness, a watcher with a much longer debounce, or a permission gate silently blocking the hook's command execution. Recorded as PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED with an open root cause, not resolved to a single explanation without further evidence.

Only a fresh session (or an environment capability this session cannot test) could confirm whether SessionStart-time hook loading (proven working via launcher-settings.json) succeeds where mid-session file-watcher reload does not.

capabilities.capability: Session transcript file as an execution-intelligence data source
capabilities.status: UNSUPPORTED (by design choice, not technical impossibility)
capabilities.evidence: /root/.claude/projects/.../<session-id>.jsonl exists, 1928 lines, and DOES contain assistant message entries with a 'thinking' content block. In the sampled entry the thinking string was empty with only an opaque 'signature' field populated — confirming no readable hidden reasoning is exposed even if this file were parsed.
limitations: This is Claude Code's internal, undocumented, versioned transcript format, not a stable public API. Building durable tooling on top of it would be fragile across Claude Code versions.
The file lives on the container's local ephemeral disk (/dev/vda) and does NOT survive session/container teardown — confirmed via `df -h`.
Per the project's own non-negotiable rule (never reconstruct hidden reasoning), this file is not used as an evidence source by any script in this project.
